### Executive Summary

This document provides a comprehensive architecture plan for a **highly advanced physics-based card drive and drift game**. The game combines realistic car physics simulation (Pacejka tire model, slip angle dynamics, weight transfer) with a strategic card system where cards modify vehicle physics parameters in real-time. The target platform is **web-based (WebGL/WebGPU)** for maximum accessibility, with potential for desktop wrapper via Electron/Tauri.

---

## 1. Technology Stack & Justification

### 1.1 Core Technologies

| Layer | Technology | Version | Justification |
|-------|------------|---------|---------------|
| **Rendering** | Three.js | ^0.169.0 | Mature WebGL abstraction, excellent ecosystem, WebGPU support via `three-webgpu`, massive community, good TypeScript support |
| **Physics** | Cannon-es | ^0.20.0 | Active fork of Cannon.js, ES modules, TypeScript types, deterministic simulation, good vehicle API (RaycastVehicle) |
| **Alternative Physics** | Ammo.js (via @pmndrs/ammo) | ^0.0.10 | Bullet Physics port, more accurate but heavier; fallback for complex collisions |
| **Game Loop** | Custom fixed-timestep loop | - | Deterministic physics requires fixed timestep (1/60s) with interpolation |
| **State Management** | Zustand | ^4.5.0 | Lightweight, TypeScript-first, no boilerplate, good for game state |
| **UI Framework** | React | ^18.3.0 | Component-based UI for card system, deck builder, HUD; concurrent features for smooth rendering |
| **React 3D** | @react-three/fiber | ^8.15.0 | React renderer for Three.js, declarative 3D, excellent performance |
| **React 3D Physics** | @react-three/cannon | ^6.6.0 | React bindings for Cannon-es, integrates with R3F |
| **Styling** | Tailwind CSS | ^3.4.0 | Utility-first, small bundle, dark mode, responsive design for HUD/menus |
| **Animation** | Framer Motion | ^11.0.0 | Card transitions, UI animations, gesture handling |
| **Input** | Custom Input Manager | - | Keyboard, gamepad (Gamepad API), touch support with deadzone handling |
| **Audio** | Tone.js | ^14.7.77 | Web Audio API wrapper, synthesis for engine sounds, spatial audio |
| **Build Tool** | Vite | ^5.4.0 | Fast HMR, optimized production builds, WASM support for physics |
| **Language** | TypeScript | ^5.5.0 | Type safety critical for physics math, card effects, game state |
| **Testing** | Vitest + Playwright | ^2.0.0 / ^1.40.0 | Unit/integration (Vitest), E2E (Playwright) |
| **Linting** | ESLint + Prettier | ^8.57.0 / ^3.2.0 | Code quality, consistent formatting |
| **Package Manager** | pnpm | ^9.0.0 | Fast, disk-efficient, strict dependency resolution |

### 1.2 Architecture Pattern

**Entity Component System (ECS) Lite** — Custom lightweight ECS for game entities (Car, Track, Particles, Cards) with:
- **Entities**: Unique IDs
- **Components**: Data-only (Transform, PhysicsBody, CarSpecs, CardEffects, ParticleEmitter)
- **Systems**: Logic processors (PhysicsSystem, InputSystem, CardSystem, AudioSystem, RenderSystem)

This avoids heavy ECS libraries (like bitecs) while providing clean separation for physics-card interaction.

### 1.3 Why Web-Based?
- **Zero-install distribution** — critical for card game virality
- **Cross-platform** — desktop, mobile, potential console via WebView
- **Easy multiplayer** — WebRTC/WebSocket for future PvP
- **Hot-reload development** — Vite HMR with physics state preservation
- **WebGPU ready** — Three.js r169+ supports WebGPU backend for future performance gains

  utilityMagnitude?: number;
  
  // Triggered
  trigger?: TriggerType;
  triggerCondition?: string;   // Expression: "driftAngle > 30 && speed > 20"

  maxTriggers?: number;        // Max activations

## 2. Technology Choices with Justification

### Core Stack

| Technology | Version | Justification |
|------------|---------|---------------|
| **TypeScript** | 5.4.2 | Strong typing essential for physics calculations; catches errors at compile time; excellent IDE support; mature ecosystem |
| **Vite** | 5.2.0 | Sub-100ms HMR critical for tuning physics parameters; esbuild-based bundling; native ESM; rollup for production |
| **Three.js** | r160 | Industry-standard WebGL renderer; extensive documentation; cannon-es integration; shader support for advanced effects |
| **Cannon-es** | 0.20.0 | TypeScript-native physics; deterministic simulation for reproducible drift mechanics; ~40KB gzipped; active maintenance |
| **Vitest** | 1.6.0 | Native ESM/TypeScript support; shares Vite config; parallel test execution; coverage reporting |

### Secondary Dependencies

| Technology | Version | Purpose |
|------------|---------|---------|
| @types/three | r160 | Three.js TypeScript definitions |
| @types/cannon-es | 0.20.0 | Cannon-es TypeScript definitions |
| gl-matrix | 4.0.1 | High-performance matrix/vector math |
| howler.js | 2.2.4 | Cross-browser audio with Web Audio API fallback |
| dat.gui | 0.7.9 | Debug UI for physics parameter tuning |
| lil-gui | 0.19.0 | Modern dat.gui replacement |

### Justification Deep-Dive

**Cannon-es over Ammo.js/Bullet**: Ammo.js requires Emscripten compilation, adds 1MB+ to bundle, and has complex TypeScript bindings. Cannon-es provides adequate precision for arcade-style drifting while maintaining 60fps on mid-range devices. The deterministic nature ensures card effects produce consistent results across sessions.

**Three.js over Babylon.js**: Three.js has larger community, more examples, and better integration with Cannon-es. Babylon.js is excellent but adds unnecessary complexity for this project's scope.

**Vite over Webpack**: Physics tuning requires rapid iteration. Vite's HMR updates in ~50ms vs Webpack's 2-5 seconds. This difference compounds over hundreds of tuning sessions.

## 10. Security Considerations

### Authentication
- Optional backend uses JWT tokens (RS256)
- Token expiry: 24 hours
- Refresh tokens stored HttpOnly

### Authorization
- Leaderboard submissions require signature verification
- HMAC-SHA256 with server-side secret
- Rate limiting: 10 submissions/hour per player

### Input Validation
- All physics parameters clamped to safe ranges
- Card effects validated against whitelist
- Network inputs sanitized (if backend enabled)

### XSS Prevention
- No innerHTML usage; textContent only
- CSP headers in production
- Sanitize any user-generated content

## 11. Performance Considerations

### Rendering
- Instanced rendering for repeated objects
- Frustum culling enabled
- LOD (Level of Detail) for distant vehicles
- Texture compression (KTX2/Basis)

### Physics
- Fixed timestep (60Hz) for determinism
- Sleep thresholds for inactive bodies
- Broadphase: SAP (Sweep and Prune)
- Collision layers to reduce checks

### Memory
- Object pooling for particles/effects
- Asset lazy loading
- Texture atlasing
- Audio sprite system

### Network (if applicable)
- Debounced leaderboard updates
- Compressed JSON responses
- CDN for static assets
